title: James Lounger #23 Session Persistence and Storage Source Audit

discarded_hypothesis.name: PLAYER_DAD_TWO_FACE_MEMORY_MIXING
discarded_hypothesis.reason: The player and James use separate physical pods and distinct session endpoints. No shared memory slot or cross-session autobiographical alias was identified. The previously observed face-generation relationship is kept separate from Vault 112 memory architecture.

gate.question: Does Lounger #23 preserve any James-specific state after James exits Tranquility Lane, and does that persistence establish a memory-storage source suitable for SAVE JAMES?
gate.passed: James has a dedicated Lounger #23 monitor, Dad-specific status/stress records and a distinct Doc simulation representation; secondary transcript documentation reports that the Lounger #23 monitor entries remain after James leaves Tranquility Lane.
gate.open: The persisted material visible at Lounger #23 is physiological/session telemetry and identification metadata. No shipped evidence reviewed proves that autobiographical memory, engram state or a removable carrier remains bound to Lounger #23 after exit.

status_record.warning: Possible program corruption. Unable to verify Resident ID. Please consult a supervisor.

stress_record.warning: Possible program corruption. Unable to verify Resident ID. Please consult a supervisor.

post_exit_persistence.finding: A legacy Vault 112 terminal transcript explicitly notes that the Lounger #23 monitor entries stay after James leaves Tranquility Lane.
post_exit_persistence.interpretation: The system retains a James-specific monitor/session binding after the active simulation session ends.
post_exit_persistence.save_james_relevance: This is the first James-specific post-exit persistence marker found, but it is not yet the required memory-state persistence source.

resident_id_642_collision_audit.candidate: Some modern terminal transcripts render Lounger #23 as 'RESIDENT ID: 642 -- UNKNOWN', while T. Dithers is also Resident ID 642.
resident_id_642_collision_audit.conflicting_evidence: A legacy/raw-oriented Vault 112 terminal transcript renders James's Lounger #23 simply as 'RESIDENT ID: UNKNOWN' with no 642 value.
resident_id_642_collision_audit.rule: Do not claim Dithers/James resident-ID aliasing or storage-slot collision until direct Fallout3.esm/xEdit evidence resolves the transcript discrepancy.
resident_id_642_collision_audit.effect: No Dithers->James memory-carrier inference is promoted from the apparent 642 collision.

dad_pod_script.finding: The Dad pod script only gates activation and exposes no persistence/storage operation.

mq04_script.finding: The quest controller tracks PlayerInTL, DadInfo, DadDogInfo, NPCReset, SafetyLock and related orchestration state, but no James-specific memory-storage handle is exposed.

exit_script.finding: On return to physical Vault 112, the script sets PlayerInTL to 0, opens Dad and player pod shells separately, clears James ghost/unconscious state and reevaluates James's package; no memory export or deletion of Dad monitor data is exposed.

save_james_effect.improvement: James-specific state demonstrably survives the TL exit at least at the monitor/session metadata layer.
save_james_effect.reason: Telemetry/session persistence does not prove autobiographical-memory persistence or carrier binding.

allowed: Lounger #23 is a James-specific physical/session endpoint.
James-specific monitor data remains available after James leaves Tranquility Lane according to documented terminal observation.
This establishes session/telemetry persistence, not a whole-person or memory backup.
not_allowed: Lounger #23 canonically stores James's complete memories after exit.
Resident ID 642 proves James and Dithers share a storage slot.
James's memory chip can already be removed from Lounger #23.
SAVE JAMES is now a vanilla executable path.

next_gate.name: JAMES_LOUNGER23_PERSISTENCE_LAYER_TO_BRAUN_MEMORY_STORAGE_BRIDGE_AUDIT
targets: Resolve the exact Fallout3.esm terminal DESC for Vault112PodTermDad to settle the Resident ID 642 discrepancy.
Inspect placed-reference and terminal-linkage data around Lounger #23 for hidden child refs, linked containers, enable parents or storage objects.
Determine whether Dad-specific status/stress NOTE records are static display assets or dynamically selected from a resident/session state source.
Search Braun/Betty reset and per-user memory-control paths for a source handle that can target Lounger #23 after James exits.
Search for any James-specific post-exit memory/engram/state object distinct from physiological telemetry.
If such a state object or storage binding is found, promote SAVE JAMES to PERSISTED_JAMES_MEMORY_STATE_RECONSTRUCTION.
